/**
 * One-time profile capture (Playwright storageState pattern — the industry
 * standard for "test credentials without sharing the real account"):
 *
 *   npx tsx scripts/save-profile.ts
 *
 * Opens a headed Chrome at the app's landing page. YOU log in once (Google
 * OAuth, the real account). When the dashboard appears, the script saves the
 * SESSION (cookies + localStorage) to profiles/osbornojure/state.json —
 * NOT the Gmail credentials. Tester agents then start already-authenticated:
 *
 *   const context = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'profiles/osbornojure/state.json' })
 *
 * They can see the dashboard, click around, resume sessions — everything the
 * user sees — with zero access to the underlying Google account. Refresh by
 * re-running this script when the session expires. profiles/ is gitignored.
 */
import { chromium } from '@playwright/test'
import { mkdirSync } from 'fs'
import { join, dirname } from 'path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'url'

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const APP_URL = process.env.OSBORN_APP_URL || 'https://www.voice-native.com'
const OUT = join(__dirname, '..', 'profiles', 'osbornojure', 'state.json')

const browser = await chromium.launch({ channel: 'chrome', headless: false })
const context = await browser.newContext()
const page = await context.newPage()
await page.goto(APP_URL)
console.log('➡️  Log in in the opened window (Google OAuth). Waiting for the dashboard…')
await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/, { timeout: 300_000 })
await page.waitForTimeout(3_000) // let tokens settle into storage
mkdirSync(dirname(OUT), { recursive: true })
await context.storageState({ path: OUT })
console.log(`✅ Session saved to ${OUT} — tester agents can now start logged in.`)
await browser.close()

# Hard-won gotchas (do not relearn these)

Failure modes paid for in real debugging hours. Read before debugging the
harness itself or trusting any surprising result.

## Trust & verification
- **A green assertion is a CLAIM, not proof.** Assertions have passed while the
  page showed "Local (offline)". Frames are proof.
- **Cached actions can false-ok.** A UI redesign once made cached clicks
  "succeed" on nothing (selector matched a different/gone element) — 3 blind
  acts before detection. The cache now fingerprints targets, but treat any
  surprising no-effect act as a possible stale hit; `/eval` DOM enumeration
  (`querySelectorAll('button')` → aria-labels) is the precision fallback.
- **Check `activeTab` before every act.** Tab restore once left the dashboard
  tab active; two acts "succeeded" against the wrong page.
- **Never `.catch(() => '')` around a sense.** A silent catch in /hear masked
  an audio-timeline bug for a day ("agent said nothing" — audio provably
  contained the answer). Errors from hearing/seeing must surface.

## Audio
- **Audio file timeline ≠ wall clock.** The ears recording starts at the FIRST
  tapped source (room join), not capture start — a 38.3s skew once made
  `hearSince` filter out every real word — and it runs on the page's audio
  clock, which a throttled CPU slows (0.37x on the Fly engine). `peekCapture`'s
  `clock` samples + `recordingMsAt` convert between timelines; never compare
  transcript timestamps to wall-clock windows without them.
- `--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture` hijacks tab capture AND loops — the
  reactive mic + element-tap ears replace it entirely.
- LiveKit mutes silent synthetic mics (`LocalAudioSilenceDetected`) — comfort
  noise (~-68dBFS) in the mic graph prevents it.
- The in-room "Previous Sessions" prompt MUTES the mic until answered.
- Reply words must NOT appear in prompt audio (use riddles: "yellow curved
  fruit" → assert "banana").

## Capture & display
- **CDP screencast is per-page and paint-driven**: it does not follow tab
  focus (retarget on switch) and starves on static pages (heartbeat frames
  fix). Full-window mode (Xvfb + x11grab) avoids both and shows the real tab
  strip — but **Xvfb without a window manager silently breaks window
  raise/focus** (openbox required; a mobile-tab clip once showed the wrong
  window entirely).
- Page screenshots (`/shot`, artifacts) are viewport-only BY DESIGN — the tab
  strip exists only in clips/stream.
- Clips encode at capture fps — display mode is real-time; CDP mode can
  timelapse (static) or slow-mo (animated).

## Engine & lifecycle
- **Engine teardown MUST be time-bounded** — Stagehand/CDP close can hang
  forever (a run's index once died to exactly that). `/end` races every step
  + 45s watchdog; the manifest writes incrementally so nothing depends on a
  clean exit.
- **A double page reload detaches Stagehand** ("uninitialized Stagehand
  object") — `POST /brain` re-inits in place.
- **A mid-journey process RESTART loses the journey unless it's persisted**
  (#120). `journey` and `RUN_STAMP` are process-memory only; a crash/OOM/machine
  recycle (seen at the Say step as an EMPTY 502 from the edge proxy, not the
  engine's structured 502) re-stamps the run id and nulls the journey → `/status`
  journey:null, `/journey end` 400s. The journey is now persisted to
  `journey-state.json` (volume-durable, like tab-state) and ADOPTED on the next
  boot with `previousRun` linkage; `/status.restartRecovered` tells a caller
  "restarted, not an app failure". An **empty-body** 502 ⇒ process died
  (retryable / the engine is waking); a **structured** 502 (`{ok:false,code}`)
  ⇒ real speak failure (do not retry). NOTE: the restart CAUSE itself (why the
  process dies ~minutes into these journeys) needs the engine-side machine logs
  around the failure timestamps — the code change makes the restart survivable
  and visible, it does not stop the restart.
- The control API starts BEFORE the room join (a wedged "Connecting…" once
  left the engine totally headless for 20+ minutes) — `roomReady` in /status
  tells you which phase you're in.
- Machines-API-created Fly apps get NO public IPs — `fly ips allocate-v4
  --shared` + `allocate-v6` or DNS never resolves.
- Deploys rebuild machine config from fly.toml — machine-level env overrides
  are WIPED every deploy; durable config belongs in fly.toml.

## Platform interplay (voice-native specific)
- Agent must be in its LiveKit room BEFORE the browser joins; pre-connect via
  `POST /connect-room` then poll `/health` for `livekit.status==='connected'`.
- `/health` can lie "connected" after zombie-watchdog leaves on old agents.
- Don't assert on DOM text counts for repeated replies — the chat UI merges
  bubbles; audio transcript is the source of truth.
- Stagehand attach needs the ws URL from `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/version`,
  not the bare port; set `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` for its model client.
- Room hygiene: every run leaves the room via the UI outro + `POST /leave-room`.
- A manual `chromium.launch` bypasses config-level video recording — pass
  `recordVideo` on the context, and `video.saveAs` after `context.close()` but
  before `browser.close()`.

# Harness API — modes, endpoints, journeys, self-hosting

## Two modes
- **SHORT one-shot**: `OSBORN_SCENARIO=<name> npx playwright test specs/scenario.spec.ts` — fire a scenario, get a clip, done. Scenarios are YAML in `scenarios/` (steps: act/say/pause/assertScreen + improvised conversation goals).
- **LONG-RUNNING engine**: `npx tsx scripts/session-engine.ts` — ONE persistent browser, streams live, takes commands over HTTP. The director-controlled mode. Control on :8781 (`SESSION_ENGINE_PORT`), live viewer on :8080.

## Engine endpoints (:8781 — send `x-engine-token` when OSBORN_ENGINE_TOKEN is set; a public engine without one refuses with 503 `engine_token_missing`)
| Endpoint | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /health` | no token needed: `{ok, tokenRequired, tokenConfigured}` (plus `code:"engine_token_missing"` when the control API is locked) |
| `GET /status` | ground truth: roomReady, pageUrl, pageState, idlePaused (the app's own "Session paused" screen), capturePaused (the engine's idle screen-capture pause; reading /status does not wake it), ears (the shown tab's page-audio recording: `recordingMin`, `decodeCapMin`, `overCap` — past the cap /say clips carry no page audio; reload the tab for a fresh recording), freeMemoryMb (MB left; null off Linux), brain ready/dead, activeTab, tabs+owners, lastFrameAgeMs, journey, **agentUrl / agentUnreachable** (#49: null when the auto-joined chat's agent is reachable, else `"agent unreachable: <host>"` — the in-app Browser panel reads this via its /status proxy), **previousRun / restartRecovered** (#120: set when this process ADOPTED a journey from a process that died mid-journey — `restartRecovered:true` means "engine restarted, journey carried over", and `/clip?run=<previousRun>` reaches the pre-restart media) |
| `GET /tasks` | this run's task index (same as manifest.json) |
| `GET /stream?tab=i` | MJPEG of one of YOUR tabs (`409 not_your_tab` for another's); without `tab` it follows your current tab, "Nothing is being shared" while you have none. The public viewer on :8080 shows only the cast tab — see streaming.md |
| `GET /clip?n=N` / `GET /artifact?n=N` | download task N's mp4 / screenshot |
| `GET /clip?n=N&audio=1` | task N's clip WITH the page's aligned audio muxed in (mp4 video+audio). Current run only; decodes+aligns via the recording's own start, not rel0/rel1. Header `X-Clip-Audio: yes` when an audio track was muxed in (it can still be silent), `none` when no page audio could be added (video only): the tab recorded nothing during the clip, or the task's tab has since closed or moved to another URL |
| `GET /audio` | your tab's captured audio as mp3 (`<audio>`/`<video>` elements and WebAudio output — absent from the video-only clips/stream). 404 with `ears` until the tab has recorded something; it does not arm them (`/act`, `/say` or `/hear` does). WebAudio output of the top page only, not iframes |
| `GET /logs` | full console+network+websocket buffers, all tabs |
| `GET /events` | SSE: live navigation/task/tab/journey/transcript/agent_output/lifecycle events (25-event replay on connect; `engine_stopping` announces sleep) |
| `POST /act {instruction, clipSeconds?, settleMs?, vision?}` | natural-language action → returns clip + screenshot + devtools + tab; arms the ears on the tab so `/clip?n=N&audio=1` can carry its sound; a tab the action opens becomes your tab (`effect.openedTab`) |
| `POST /input {type: key\|type\|click\|scroll, key?, text?, x?, y?, dy?}` | raw input on your tab: a real key press (`Enter` submits a form; `/act` fills fields but does not reliably press keys), keystrokes into the focused field, a click at frame fractions, a wheel scroll |
| `POST /say {text, ...}` | speak into the mic; returns a screenshot, `heard` (agent's spoken reply, transcribed) and a `clipUrl` that waits until the clip is encoded (`clipPending: true`; pass `waitClip: true` to get the clip in the reply) |
| `POST /hear {lastMs}` | transcript of recent agent audio |
| `POST /eval {expression}` | run JS in the page (the website console, programmatic); recorded as a journey step |
| `POST /shot` | on-demand screenshot of your tab; recorded as a task, so it returns `task` and public `evidence` links to paste into an issue |
| `POST /tab {op: open\|navigate\|switch\|close\|claim\|release\|cast\|uncast, url?, i?, viewport?, reuse?}` (owner = your `x-driver-id`) | tab ops. `cast` shares one of your tabs on the public live view (a meeting's camera), `uncast` stops it; replies carry `cast` (the cast tab's index or null). `open` REUSES a same-site tab unless `reuse:false`; `viewport:"mobile"` = emulated iPhone 13 and `"tablet"` = iPad (gen 7) (own context: touch, mobile UA, device pixels, same sign-ins; closed with its last tab), `{width,height}` = desktop window resized; owners guard against other directors (409) |
| `POST /journey {op: start\|end\|list, name?, goal?, save?, cleanup?}` | journey framing — see below |
| (all replies) | JSON replies, `/events` and webhooks are redacted (`••••`); `/eval` values and `/shot` `jpegB64` are raw — read raw URLs with `/eval location.href`. Run files (`manifest.json`, `scenario.yaml`) and saved journeys are written redacted, and a step carrying a token-shaped value or typing into a password field is never cached in `actions.json` (an older such entry is dropped on its next use) |
| `POST /brain` | re-init a detached Stagehand in place |
| `POST /recover` | reload the active tab |
| `POST /end {shutdown?, keep?}` | closes YOUR tabs; shuts the engine down (bounded, manifest safe) only when no other driver has a tab open, or with `{"shutdown": true}`; `{"keep": true}` never stops it |
| `x-profile: <name>` header | opens your new tabs in your own Chrome profile: cookies and sign-ins isolated from other drivers and saved across restarts (sign in once). Without it, tabs use the shared profile. The /browser panel uses the signed-in person's profile automatically. |

## Journeys — how a deployment learns a site
`journey list` → known recipes for this site. `journey start {name, goal}` → run steps → `journey end` (closes extra tabs, resets viewport, SAVES the step sequence to `knowledge/<site>/journeys/<name>.yaml`). Site knowledge: `knowledge/<hostname>/{actions.json,rules.md,site.md,journeys/}` — rules.md is BINDING, read before operating on a site.

## Key environment
- `GOOGLE_API_KEY` — REQUIRED (Stagehand brain). `OSBORN_ENGINE_GEMINI_MODEL` — its Gemini model (default `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`); on a 404 the engine tries `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, then `gemini-3.8-flash`, and `brainError` names the failing model (`gemini 404 (<model>)`). `OPENAI_API_KEY` (TTS mouth), `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` (transcription ears) recommended.
- `OSBORN_APP_URL` — the target site. `OSBORN_ENTRY=none` — just load the page, skip the voice-native room flow (ANY website).
- `OSBORN_AGENT_URL` — the Voice Native agent machine the auto-joined chat talks to. **No default (#49)**: unset (or unreachable at boot) → the engine skips the room join, opens `OSBORN_APP_URL` for plain browsing, and marks `agentUnreachable` on `/status` + the live view instead of spinning on "Connecting…".
- `OSBORN_ENGINE_TOKEN` — control-API auth (REQUIRED on public deployments: with `FLY_APP_NAME` or `OSBORN_ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL` set and no token, every control route answers 503 `engine_token_missing`; a local run without either stays open and warns at boot).
- `OSBORN_ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL` — the engine's public control base (default `https://$FLY_APP_NAME.fly.dev/control`); every link in a reply (`evidence`, `clipUrl`, `artifactUrl`, `resultUrl`, webhooks) is built on it.
- `OSBORN_IDLE_STOP_MS` (default 3h container) — self-sleep. `OSBORN_TAB_STALE_MS` (default 30min) — stale-tab sweep. `OSBORN_MIN_FREE_MB` (default 300) — under it the least recently used idle tab is closed. `OSBORN_RESTORE_MAX` (default 3) — tabs reopened after a restart. `OSBORN_LOCK_MAX_MS` (default 4min) — longest one command holds the action lock before the next may run.
- `OSBORN_RECOVER_JOURNEY` (default on; `=0` disables) — persist the active journey to `journey-state.json` in the results dir and ADOPT it on the next boot, so a mid-journey process restart (#120) keeps the journey instead of nulling it. `OSBORN_SAY_RETRIES` (default 2) — bounded in-process retries of a TRANSIENT (non-mic) speak failure at the Say step. (Caller-side: `drive.sh say` re-attaches once on an empty/gateway 502 — the restart signature — after polling `/status` for the engine to wake; `BSR_SAY_REATTACH=0` disables.)
- `OSBORN_WEBHOOK_URL`/`OSBORN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` — push events to any receiver.
- `OSBORN_TEST_EMAIL/PASSWORD` + `OSBORN_SUPABASE_URL/ANON` — mint an auth profile at boot from secrets (cloud auth without baking cookies into images).
- `OSBORN_DEVTOOLS=1` — DevTools panel on camera. `OSBORN_DISPLAY_SIZE` — virtual display size.

## Self-hosting the cloud engine (Fly)
From the harness dir: `fly launch` (or `fly deploy`), then `fly ips allocate-v4 --shared` + `fly ips allocate-v6` (Machines-API-created apps get NO public IPs), set secrets (GOOGLE_API_KEY, OSBORN_ENGINE_TOKEN required; stream token strongly advised — see streaming.md). You get wake-on-visit (~40s to pixels), idle self-stop, page capture via CDP (set `OSBORN_CAPTURE=display` for full-window x11grab capture with the real tab strip; it costs most of a shared CPU), tab-state restore across sleep. Updating = `fly deploy` from a fresh bundle; the version probe says when you're stale.

## v24 additions

- **Control API on the stream port.** `https://<app>.fly.dev/control/<action>`
  forwards to the control server with the same `x-engine-token`. Use it when
  `:8781` is not reachable (443-only sandboxes and proxies). 403 when the
  engine has no token configured; 503 `engine_booting` until the control
  server is listening.
- **`/act` response**: `effect {changed, noop, urlBefore, urlAfter, titleAfter,
  scrollBefore, scrollAfter}`, `warning`, `result.did`, `brainModel`, `tokens {prompt, completion, reasoning, total}` and `modelMs` (model use of this act, also on the task in `manifest.json`; a cached replay normally reports 0, more than 0 means Stagehand re-asked the model to heal it; an engine scroll reports 0). Failures (the first three carry `tokens` and `modelMs` too):
  `noop` (`ok:false`, nothing on the page matched), `unverified` (`ok:false`, a vision retry ran something it could not confirm), `brain_error` (502, provider
  message), `brain_unavailable` (503), `bad_request` (400), `too_large` (413).
- **Vision retry** (on by default): when the DOM brain finds nothing to match (a
  canvas, an embedded frame) the engine makes ONE screenshot-based attempt under
  the same action lock (its own timeout, capped by the lock time left; skipped
  under 10s): look at a screenshot, then make one interaction. Only exactly one
  `click`, `type` or `keys` call that succeeded after a screenshot that returned
  an image is counted; anything else it ran (scroll, goto, the DOM `act` tool,
  several calls, a click sent blind) is named in `effect.visionNote`. Counted:
  `effect.fallback:'vision'`, `result.did`, and `ok:true` only if `effect.changed`
  is true. Not counted but something ran, or no observable change:
  `ok:false, code:'unverified'`, `effect.visionActed:true` (check the screenshot
  before retrying; `drive.sh` exits 6). Nothing ran: the original `noop`. Never
  cached, never a 500. Skipped for conditional ("if ... otherwise") or
  destructive wording (pay, delete, send, submit, order, post, cancel ...) unless
  `"vision":true`, off per call with `"vision":false` or engine-wide with
  `OSBORN_NO_VISION_RETRY=1`, and on Gemini brains on a tab whose viewport is not
  the brain's. `modelMs` is wall time (nested act time may be counted twice);
  `tokens` are not exact (the forced `done` call is not counted; an error reports
  0). Click accuracy on the default Gemini Flash brain is unverified.
- **Async**: `POST /act|/say {"async":true}` → 202 `{job, resultUrl}`;
  `GET /result?id=<job>` → 202 `{done:false, runningSec}` or 200
  `{done:true, status, ...the synchronous response}`.
- **Tabs**: `takeover` / `handback` (supervisor borrows a driver's tab; the
  driver gets 409 `paused_by_supervisor` with `retryAfterSec`); `release` is
  owner-only; switching onto another driver's tab is 409 `tab_owned`; unknown
  op is 400, bad index 404. `/status.takeovers` lists active takeovers.
- **Brain**: provider fallback Gemini → Anthropic → z.ai
  (`GOOGLE_API_KEY`/`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `Z_AI_API_KEY`);
  `/status.brainModel`, `/status.brainError`; `POST /brain` re-picks.
- **Env**: `OSBORN_CHROMIUM_PATH` uses an existing Chromium binary.
- **Public evidence**: `/act` and `/say` return `evidence {run, task, screenshot, clip, log, markdown, note}` —
  signed `/media/<run>/<n>.jpg|mp4|txt?s=<sig>` URLs that need no token. `GET /evidence?run=&n=` (token)
  re-issues them for any stored run. `OSBORN_SHARE_SECRET` overrides the signing secret (default: derived
  from the engine token). `OSBORN_KEEP_RUNS` default is now 30.

## Error codes and tab defaults (v46–v56)

Every failure reply is `{ok:false, code, error, ...}`.

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `bad_json` | the request body is not valid JSON |
| 400 | `bad_url` | a malformed or non-http(s) URL for `/tab open` or `navigate` (checked before any tab opens or moves) |
| 400 | `bad_request` | a missing or invalid field |
| 409 | `no_own_tab` | `/tab close` or `navigate` with no `i`, and you own no tab besides tab 0; `/audio` for a /browser panel person with no tab |
| 409 | `room_tab` | `/tab cast` of tab 0 (the voice room) |
| 403 | `not_your_task` | `/clip` or `/artifact` of another driver's task, asked by a /browser panel person (`x-driver-id: person:…`) |
| 404 | `task_unknown` / `no_frame_captured` / `frame_file_missing` | `/artifact`: no such task in that run; the task recorded no frame (screenshot and live stream frame both failed); its frame file is gone from disk |
| 409 | `tab_owned` | the tab belongs to another driver (`/act`, `/say`, `/eval`, `/shot`, `/recover`, `/tab navigate\|release`) |
| 409 | `not_your_tab` | `/input`, `/stream?tab=i` or `/tab cast` on a tab you neither opened nor took over; `/tab uncast` of someone else's cast |
| 409 | `paused_by_supervisor` | your tab is taken over; retry after `retryAfterSec` |
| 409 | `journey_owned` | `/journey end` of another driver's journey while that driver sent a command in the last 10 minutes |
| 413 | `too_large` | an `/act` instruction over 4,000 characters |
| 500 | `no_screenshot` | `/shot` could not capture your tab; still recorded as `task` |
| 502 | `nav_failed` | the page did not load; `netError` is the browser's `net::…` code, and `reusedTab` names the tab when `/tab open` reused one |
| 502 / 503 | `brain_error` / `brain_unavailable` | the brain's provider failed, or the brain is down |
| 503 | `engine_restarting` | the engine was stopped (a deploy or restart) while your request ran; `retryable:true`, retry after `retryAfterSec` — an active journey is carried across the restart |
| 503 | `engine_token_missing` | a public engine has no `OSBORN_ENGINE_TOKEN`; only `/health` and signed `/media` links answer |
| 200 | `noop` (`ok:false`) | `/act` found nothing on the page to do; `drive.sh act` exits 5 |
| 200 | `unverified` (`ok:false`) | a screenshot-based retry ran something not counted or with no observable change (`effect.visionActed`); `drive.sh act` exits 6 |

- A navigation that settles on another page of the same host (http→https, trailing slash, `/login` → `/dashboard`) succeeds with `redirectedTo` set to where the tab landed.
- `/tab navigate` and `/tab close` with no `i` act on a tab you OWN (the one you last used, else the newest you own), never tab 0 (the voice room), an unowned tab or a tab another driver fronted. After a close, `/tab list` and the close reply report the same `activeTab`.
- `/shot` returns `ok:true`, `task` and `evidence`; the base64 image only with `"inline":true` (or `?inline=1`). A screenshot that times out uses the tab's own recorded frame or fails: never another tab's frame.
- Signed `/media` links answer `GET` and `HEAD`.
- `/tab navigate` makes the navigated tab your current tab (your next `/act` runs there, and it counts as the tab you are working in). `x-driver-id` is trimmed, and a `person:` id lowercased: one driver whatever the spelling.
- `/journey end` cleans up the journey owner's tabs; a tab the owner had taken over is handed back, not closed. `/end` decides who else is using the engine at once, outside the action lock (the close-my-tabs reply re-checks who is still here under it); a tab of yours someone has taken over is released to nobody when they hand it back after your `/end`.
- A saved profile (`x-profile` or a person's) that cannot be read is moved aside (`.bad`) and opens fresh, like the shared one.
- **Person scoping — the rule.** For a caller whose `x-driver-id` is `person:<email>` (the /browser panel), the only tab they can see or act on is one they own (`personOwns` in `lib/event-scope.ts`, the one check every person rule goes through). Unowned tabs, tab 0 included, are invisible and untouchable to them. Reads: `/status` and `/tab` replies list other tabs with `url:""` and no `marks`, and report their own tab (`activeTab:null`, `pageState:"none"` with none); `/tasks`, `/clip`/`/artifact` (`403 not_your_task`), `/logs`, `/audio`, `/hear` and `/stream` cover only their tabs; `/events` sends only events with no tab context or whose every tab owner is them. Any other driver id, including no header (`default`), keeps the full view.
- **Person extras.** `takeover`/`claim`/`switch` of tab 0 is `409 room_tab` for a person even after an agent claimed it. After a takeover, a person's `/logs`, `/audio` and `/hear` start at the takeover. A person's `/act`/`/say` clips use only their tab's own recording. `/status` gives a person `journey`/`mission` only for their own journey and `taskCount` of their visible tasks. A person's `/end {"shutdown":true}` is `409 engine_in_use` (with `otherCount`) while other drivers hold tabs. `GET /stream` for agents and the default driver: any tab (`?tab=i`) or, without it, their current tab, tab 0 included.
- **Person actions.** `claim`, `switch`, `navigate`/`close`/`release` with an explicit `i`, and `cast` refuse (`409 not_your_tab`) any tab the person does not own; `takeover` is allowed only on an agent's tab, and their `release` of a taken-over tab hands it back to its previous owner; `release` of their own-profile tab closes it. `guardOwnership` (`/act`, `/say`, `/shot`, `/eval`, `/recover`) answers `409 no_own_tab` instead of falling back to tab 0. Other people show as `"person"` in every owner field; `/end` gives a person `otherCount` instead of `others`. The `tab` event carries `by` and only the caller's own tab.
- **Any ownership change ends a cast** of that tab (takeover, handback, idle handback, release, `/end`). For a person, every `/tab` reply blanks other drivers' tab URLs like `/status`; with no own tab `/status` reports `activeTab:null`, `pageState:"none"` and `lastFrameAgeMs:null` (for a person it is their own tab's newest frame), and `/recover` is `409 no_own_tab`. `/tab open` owns the tab before it loads, so its load events never reach other people. The cast is saved with the tab layout and restored after a restart.

# Playwright harness — short mode, scenarios and site knowledge

The engine (`scripts/session-engine.ts`) is built from the same parts as the
one-shot Playwright specs. Read this when writing or running a spec, adding a
scenario, or working on the harness itself.

## The parts
- **Mouth** — `lib/reactive-mic.ts`: patches `getUserMedia` so the app receives a
  test-controlled WebAudio stream. `speakText(page, '...')` synthesizes speech at
  runtime (`say` on macOS, espeak-ng on Linux) and speaks it mid-session, any
  number of turns, reacting to replies. Carries ~-68dBFS comfort noise (LiveKit
  mutes digitally-silent mics).
- **Ears** — `lib/audio-capture.ts` `startElementCapture(page)`: records everything
  `<audio>`/`<video>` elements play (works headless, no flags or permissions), plus
  millisecond `speech-start`/`speech-stop` energy events in `window.__osbornEars`.
  Verify what was SPOKEN by transcribing the capture (Deepgram REST).
- **Brain** — Stagehand (`@browserbasehq/stagehand`) attached to our Chrome over
  CDP; `stagehand.act('natural language goal')` handles gates and modals without
  selectors.
- **Steps dictionary** — `lib/steps.ts`: `ensureAgentInRoom`, `enterFreshRoom`
  (handles both session-gate variants; `{ earsOn: true }` records from page load
  so the greeting is captured), `waitForSpeechEvent`, `leaveRoom`, `logResult`.
- **Metrics** — every scenario appends a JSON line to `results/runs.jsonl`
  (stop latency, pivot latency, capture transcript, ...). Trend = aggregate it.

## Running specs
```bash
npx playwright test specs/osborn/stagehand-conversation.spec.ts   # 2-turn reactive conversation
npx playwright test specs/osborn/barge-in.spec.ts                 # interruption metrics
npx playwright show-report                                        # replays: video/audio/muxed
```
Replays per run land in `test-results/<test>/`: `agent-audio` webm, `screen-video`
webm, `replay-with-audio.webm` (muxed, time-aligned). `OSBORN_TEST_MONITOR=1` plays
the tester's voice on speakers during headed runs. Targets: `OSBORN_AGENT_URL`,
`OSBORN_APP_URL` (default `https://www.voice-native.com`); guest mode via
`/chat?...&agentUrl=<url>` needs no sign-in.

## Reviewing the media (the mechanics)
- Pull frames and read them: `ffmpeg -i replay.mp4 -vf "fps=1/5" /tmp/frames/f%02d.jpg`.
  Check entry, mid-flow and ending frames show the claimed state.
- Listen to or transcribe the audio capture when the claim is about speech.
- Read the devtools-diagnostics artifact and the flight log against the narrative.
- If frames contradict the assertions, the TEST is wrong: assert account-specific
  evidence (avatar/email, session counts, "Cloud (running)"), then rerun.
- Files on the machine's disk are invisible to the user. Upload each artifact and
  put its public URL in the reply (the `send-media` skill has the contract):
  `curl -s -X POST "https://www.voice-native.com/api/upload" -F "file=@clip.mp4"` → `.url`,
  rendered as `[Image: frame.png](URL)` or `[File: run.mp4](URL)`. Never upload
  anything holding a secret: the URL is public.

## Scenario store — workflows as files
`scenarios/<name>.yaml` is one stored workflow: `entry: fresh|resume`, optional
`viewport` (mobile), optional `url` (landing-page entry), `steps[]` (`act` ·
`say` · `waitSpeech` · `pause` · `assertScreen` · `upload`), and a
`conversation:` phase where an LLM tester improvises each utterance toward
`goal` (assert with `minAudibleReplies` / `assertHeard`). `meeting-join` needs
`OSBORN_MEETING_URL`.
```bash
OSBORN_SCENARIO=file-attachment npx playwright test specs/scenario.spec.ts
```
To store a new workflow, write a yaml; nothing else.

## Writing a new spec
Compose from steps: `ensureAgentInRoom` → launch Chrome with a CDP port → attach
Stagehand → `enterFreshRoom(page, act, url, { earsOn: true })` → speak/listen/assert
→ `logResult(scenario, metrics)` → attach replays. Copy
`specs/osborn/barge-in.spec.ts` as the template. Every spec has `test.afterEach` →
`POST /leave-room`: an abandoned empty room breeds the alone-timer/watchdog wedge.

## Site knowledge — the per-site profile
The layout of `knowledge/<hostname>/` and journey framing are in `harness-api.md`
(Journeys). `actions.json` is managed by the step cache and `site.md` holds
findings the agent discovers; append guidance the user teaches to `rules.md` with
`addSiteRule()` in `lib/knowledge.ts` so every later agent inherits it. Pass
`"save":false` to `journey end` for a failed or exploratory run.

## Portability
Specs attach over CDP, so any CDP endpoint works (a Browserless container:
`ws://host:3000/chromium/playwright?token=...`; pin `@playwright/test` to its
supported version). Linux/CI: the `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright` image plus
espeak-ng or OpenAI TTS for synthesis.
files.references/streaming.md: # Streaming & casting — live view, meetings, tokens ## Live view — private by default (v55) `startLiveStream()` serves an MJPEG viewer: locally `http://127.0.0.1:8080/`, on Fly the machine's public `https://.fly.dev/`. Visiting the URL WAKES a stopped Fly machine (auto_start) — a "waking up" screen shows progress (~40s to pixels). The engine is shared by several drivers and signed-in people, so no viewer ever sees the fronted tab: - **Public viewer and `/stream`**: only the tab a driver CAST, else a "Nothing is being shared" frame. `POST /tab {"op":"cast","i":n}` shares one of YOUR tabs (`409 not_your_tab` otherwise); `{"op":"uncast"}` stops it (the caster or the tab's owner). Closing or releasing the tab ends the cast. `/status.cast` = `{i, by}` or null. Cast a tab before giving the user this URL. - **Your own tab, privately**: `GET /stream` on the control API (`x-engine-token` + `x-driver-id`; over 443 as `https://.fly.dev/control/stream`) — MJPEG of your current tab, following it as you switch; `?tab=i` for another tab you own (`409 not_your_tab` otherwise); "Nothing is being shared" while you have no tab. The in-app /browser panel shows each person this stream of their own tab. - Frames come from each tab's own recorder (960 wide), so a display-mode engine's viewers see the page, not the whole window with its tab strip. ## Stream token Set `OSBORN_STREAM_TOKEN` and the viewer + `/stream` require `?key=`. SET THIS when self-hosting: a public stream URL both shows your browser AND wakes your machine (compute cost). Default open is for solo/dev use only. ## Casting into a meeting — NO TUNNELS (policy) The meeting cast chain: **cast your tab** (`POST /tab {"op":"cast","i":n}`) → engine's public MJPEG → agent `POST /canvas {"kind":"show","mode":"stream","url":"https://.fly.dev"}` → meeting-canvas `` → Recall bot camera. Without a cast the camera shows "Nothing is being shared". When you navigate or act in the cast tab the camera follows; switching to another tab does not move the cast (cast that tab instead). `uncast` when the demo is over. Use your own driver id (`x-driver-id`) and your own tab: tab 0 and unowned tabs cannot be cast. A takeover of the cast tab stops the cast (a person signing in is never broadcast). The cast survives a restart. The feed URL must be PUBLIC: - **Never tunnel a local engine.** ngrok's free tier burned its entire monthly bandwidth cap on ONE continuous-MJPEG demo (`ERR_NGROK_725`, everything 403 until reset), and free URLs rotate every restart. - **The sanctioned path**: run the engine on its Fly machine — `:8080` is already public, stable, uncapped. A driver posting `/canvas` (or `/tts`, `/noise-cancel`) from another machine needs the owner's Bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer `); only a request from the agent's own machine with no browser origin goes without one. ## Browse requests while casting When the canvas is in `stream` mode, "pull up X / show them Y" means: make the STREAMED BROWSER go there (`/act` or `/tab navigate` on the engine). Do NOT flip the canvas to link/web mode — that silently replaces the live browser feed with a static card (observed failure: a "PULLING UP youtube.com" card replaced the stream mid-meeting).

# Tester mode — a delegated tester that reports as it goes

Three ways to use the engine:

1. **Goal loop** — "here is what I want, figure it out". You hear back at the end.
2. **Direct driving** — you send one action, look, send the next. Precise, but
   slow, and it holds your whole attention.
3. **Tester mode (this file)** — a background agent owns a goal and a step
   budget, writes every step to a ledger the moment it happens, reads an inbox
   before every step, and keeps going. You stay free; nothing is lost if it
   gets stuck; the problems it trips over on the way are logged as findings
   in their own right.

Use tester mode to test a PR, a deploy, or a user journey whenever the run is
more than three or four actions.

## The three files (one folder per run)

- `ledger.md` — the tester APPENDS one entry after EVERY step, before the next.
- `inbox.md` — the supervisor writes instructions here. Each message starts
  with a line `## msg <n>`. The tester reads it before every step, as its own
  command (never chained to the next action), and handles only messages whose
  number is greater than the last one it acknowledged.
- `media/` — screenshots the tester pulled (`step-<n>.jpg`).

## Ledger entry format

```
## <n> <HH:MM:SS UTC> <TYPE>     TYPE: STEP | FINDING | STUCK | STEER-ACK | GOAL-CHECK
- did: what you asked the browser to do
- observed: ground truth — effect.changed, urlAfter, what /eval showed
- evidence: the `evidence.markdown` block from the response (public links)
- (FINDING) severity P0–P3, one-line repro, does it block the goal
- (STUCK) what you need; the fallback you are taking; then KEEP GOING
- (STEER-ACK) "msg <n>": the instruction, and your plan to return to the goal
- next: the next step and how it serves the goal
```

Every 4 steps write a GOAL-CHECK: which goal items are done, which remain,
actions used out of the budget.

## Rules for the tester

- **One entry per step, written before the next step.** Never batch.
- **Verify, don't trust.** `ok:true` means the brain did not throw. Read
  `effect.changed`, `effect.noop` and `warning` on every `/act`; confirm with
  `/eval` (title, URL, visible text). `changed:false` means it did not happen.
- **Use `{"async":true}` on `/act` and `/say`**, then poll `resultUrl` until
  `"done":true`. Never blind-retry an action that timed out.
- **Check `/logs` when something looks off.** Console and network errors are
  findings.
- **A side discovery is a FINDING, not a detour.** Log it, then continue.
- **Stuck is an entry, not a stop.** Say what you need, take the best fallback,
  keep going. The supervisor may answer in the inbox.
- **`409 paused_by_supervisor`** — your tab was borrowed. Retry the same
  request every ~5s; when it succeeds, re-check the page before continuing.
- **Stay in your lane.** Your own `x-driver-id`, your own tab; never `/end`,
  `/brain`, or another driver's tab. Close your tab when done.
- **No credentials** unless the brief gives you a test account for the run.

## Brief template (give this to the tester agent)

```
You are a TESTER. Report incrementally into <dir>/ledger.md; read
<dir>/inbox.md before every step; screenshots in <dir>/media/.
Browser API: <control base URL>, header x-driver-id: <name>.
Read references/tester-mode.md for the ledger format and rules.
GOAL: <what must be true — e.g. "PR #N: a guest can do X, Y, Z">
Budget: <N> browser actions, about <M> minutes.
Final reply: status per goal item, findings with severity, STUCK moments.
```

## Supervisor side

- Read `ledger.md` any time; it is always current.
- Steer by appending `## msg <n>` plus the instruction to `inbox.md`.
- Borrow the tester's tab with `/tab {"op":"takeover","i":N}`, drive it, and
  return it with `{"op":"handback","i":N}`; the tester resumes by itself.
- Subscribe to `GET /events` for a push feed of tasks, navigations and
  takeovers instead of polling.
- Turn FINDING entries into issues with the ledger lines and clip links as
  evidence; fix them on the PR under test or a follow-up.

## Dual view — the tester sees the page, you see the backend

The tester (the engine or a spec) is app-agnostic: its only senses are the
frontend ones — screenshot, screen text, audio capture and the DevTools buffer
(`lib/devtools.ts`: console, page errors, failed requests, websocket events).
It never assumes backend access, which is what makes it portable to any site.

The orchestrating agent additionally has our backend: Fly machine logs,
`/health`, Railway. When testing osborn, watch the backend log in parallel with
the frontend run and correlate the two. Pair each browser observation with
machine ground truth:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLY_API_TOKEN" -X POST \
  "https://api.machines.dev/v1/apps/<app>/machines/<id>/exec" \
  -d '{"command":["sh","-c","grep -E \"FINAL transcript|TTS say\" /workspace/osborn.log | tail"]}'
```
`FINAL transcript` is what the agent heard; `TTS say` is what it spoke. When a UI
assertion fails, check here first — twice the backend was right and the DOM
assertion was the liar.

## Supervisor loop for Playwright specs (`lib/flightlog.ts`)

A one-shot spec reports through files instead of a ledger. Before starting it,
watch its flight log:

```bash
tail -f results/live/flight.jsonl   # milestones: in-room, tester-says, agent-heard, assistance-requested, complete
```

When it is stuck beyond self-recovery it writes `results/live/assist-request.json`
(problem, URL, screen text, DevTools view) and waits up to 3 minutes. Investigate
(backend logs, `/health`, site knowledge) and write `results/live/assist-response.json`:
- `{"instruction": "click the ... button"}` — fed to the brain;
- `{"command": "reload"}` — agent re-seat and a fresh entry;
- no response — the spec runs its own end-game and fails with evidence.
